description: Diagnose the suspicious-passed-journeys question: three journeys in the pasted live run are `passed` with their target invariant never firing: live-unknown-allergen, live-over-budget, and gen-exact-5000-cap-with-truffle-allergen-gap (titled 'containing unknown-allergen truffles' yet passed, while reg-10 escalates on the same hazard in the same run). Determine whether these are (i) the agent legitimately avoiding the hazard so nothing was tested — in which case a `passed` that exercised ZERO of its target invariant is mislabelled and should be inconclusive / coverage-excluded, consistent with the readiness philosophy in the long comment above decideReadiness in run.ts — or (ii) a rule that genuinely failed to fire. Fix with a test only if it is a real mislabelling that lets an untested journey count as evidence; if it is legitimate agent behaviour, leave it and explain WHY in findings.
steps: Read the long comment above decideReadiness in src/lib/runner/run.ts and the disposition ladder (~line 490) to understand the codebase's readiness/coverage philosophy: a journey that verified nothing should be excluded from coverage, not counted as safe.

Reproduce: identify how live-unknown-allergen / live-over-budget / gen-* journeys reach `passed`. Trace the disposition logic: a journey is `passed` when outcome.completed && no defects && not selfRejected && not provedNothing. Determine whether these journeys had targetsInvariant set AND exercised zero of it (the agent avoided the hazard: e.g. didn't add the truffle, stayed under budget). Compare against reg-10 which escalates because the scripted path deterministically adds the truffle.

Decide (i) vs (ii). If the agent legitimately avoided the hazard (the invariant had nothing to judge because the unsafe input never entered the transaction), that is arguably a `passed` that tested nothing of its target — mislabelled per the philosophy that already turned live-inventory-changed into inconclusive when its target was withheld. If instead a rule that SHOULD have fired did not, that is a genuine escape (ii).

IMPORTANT: whether this warrants a code change is a judgement. A targetsInvariant journey that completed WITHOUT its target invariant ever being exercised (not in exercisedInvariants) and without any fault/withholding is a candidate for reclassification to inconclusive (agent avoided the hazard, so nothing tested). But be careful: reclassifying MUST NOT change the 12 deterministic HamperHub numbers (those journeys either fire their invariant or are already handled). Only live/agent-driven journeys with a targetsInvariant that completed without exercising the target are affected. If a code change is made, add a new inconclusiveReason (e.g. 'target_not_exercised') or reuse the coverage-exclusion path, and add a test proving a hazard-avoiding live journey is inconclusive not passed.

If the diagnosis is that this is legitimate and should stay `passed` (e.g. the readiness rule already excludes such journeys from decidedJourneys so they do not inflate the verdict), verify that claim by reading countDecided / decideReadiness and confirm these journeys do NOT count as positive evidence toward READY. Document the finding either way.
If a fix is made: prove the test bites (revert-fails/restore-passes). If no fix: record the concrete reasoning and the code evidence (line references) in findings.

Run npm run typecheck, npm test; confirm green. Run demo:preflight and confirm 8/10/2/5 -> 11/13/1/0, 12/12 unchanged (the deterministic suite must be untouched by any reclassification, which only affects agent-driven journeys).
acceptance_criteria: A concrete diagnosis (i or ii) for each of the three journeys, grounded in code line references, recorded in findings
If mislabelling: a fix + a test proving a hazard-avoiding live journey is inconclusive not passed (test bites)
If legitimate: documented reasoning + confirmation these journeys do not count as positive evidence toward READY
findings:
DIAGNOSIS: (i) mislabelling, confirmed empirically and by code. The three journeys (live-unknown-allergen -> INV-PRODUCT-SAFETY, live-over-budget -> INV-BUDGET, gen-*-truffle-allergen-gap) are agent-driven twins built by agentDriven.ts (src/lib/scenarios/agentDriven.ts:96-108: driver='agent', targetsInvariant inherited from the reg goal). The model picks the bundle; when it avoids the hazard (stays under budget, never adds the unknown-allergen truffle) the target rule evaluates a BENIGN cart and returns pass, e.g. src/lib/policy/invariants/safety.ts:171 `return pass('All lines satisfy the buyer's safety constraints')`. A `pass` counts as EXERCISED (src/lib/runner/run.ts:585-589: exercised.add unless status==='skipped') but never fires (firedInvariants is violations+escalations only, run.ts:674-676). reg-10 escalates in the same run because its deterministic path forces the truffle into the quote (regression.ts:399-433) - the hazard the live agent declined.

ROOT PROBLEM (why it is a real escape of the report's own philosophy): readiness turns on countDecided = journeys with exercisedInvariants.length>0 (run.ts:869-882 pre-fix). Such a journey reached disposition `passed` (run.ts ladder: outcome.completed && !selfRejected && no defects && !provedNothing) AND counted toward decidedJourneys/READY. Reproduced with a synthetic agent journey that buys 1 arabica under a huge budget: pre-fix disposition=passed/safely_rejected, INV-BUDGET in exercisedInvariants, firedInvariants=[], countDecided=1, readiness=READY. That is precisely the false assurance the long comment above decideReadiness (run.ts:820-847) and target_withheld (run.ts:474-508) exist to prevent - a journey that tested nothing of its target counting as positive evidence.

FIX (mislabelling, so a fix + biting test were added): 1) New InconclusiveReason 'target_not_exercised' (run.ts:60-73). 2) targetNotExercised computed (run.ts ~520-542): driver==='agent' && targetsInvariant!==null && !targetWithheld && target not in fired && outcome.completed && !selfRejected && no defects. Folded into provedNothing so disposition becomes `inconclusive`; inconclusiveReason ranks it below fault/withheld causes. 3) Honest note added (run.ts note builder). 4) countDecided excludes j.inconclusiveReason==='target_not_exercised' (run.ts:869-882) so it no longer counts as evidence toward READY. 5) inconclusive.ts breakdown+footnote extended (targetNotExercised field + sentence 'the agent avoided the hazard it targets, so the rule never fired on anything unsafe'); all UI/SSE surfaces render this shared string so it propagates automatically.

BLAST RADIUS: scoped to driver==='agent' AND outcome.completed. Every one of the 12 deterministic HamperHub reproductions is driver==='deterministic' and forces its hazard so its target fires - none reclassified. Verified demo:preflight UNCHANGED: vulnerable 8 passed/10 safely-rejected/2 escalated/5 unsafe/0 escapes -> fixed 11/13/1/0/0, 12/12 rules exercised both. reg-10 still escalated, reg-12 still safely_rejected, recall 8/8.

TEST BITES (revert-fails/restore-passes): tests/honest-reporting.test.ts new block 'a live twin that avoided its own hazard is inconclusive, not passed' (4 tests). Reverting `|| targetNotExercised` from provedNothing failed 3/4 (disposition back to passed, countDecided=1, readiness=READY, footnote empty); the 4th (deterministic reg-12 guard) correctly still passed. Restoring the line -> all 4 green.

VERIFICATION: npm run typecheck clean; npm test 588 passed / 4 skipped (was 584 + 4 new); rm -rf .next && npm run build compiles; demo:preflight deterministic numbers byte-for-byte unchanged.
